simple.meaning: גְּנֵבָה (gᵉnêbâh) is a Hebrew word meaning “stealing , i.e. (concretely) something stolen.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: גְּנֵבָה (H1591) appears 2 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Exodus 22:2, with occurrences in Exodus.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to גְּנֵבָה (H1591) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in גְּנֵבָה (H1591) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: גְּנֵבָה (gᵉnêbâh) / H1591 is traced through Exodus 22:2, Exodus 22:3 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

definitions.full: H1591. genebah גְּנֵבָה noun feminine thing stolen (on formation compare Ba NB 161, 166 ) — גְּנֵבָה Exod 22:3 (an animal); בִּגְנֵבָתוֺ 22:2 , ׳בְּ pret. compare Di.

occurrences.englishText: If the thief is found breaking in, and is struck so that he dies, there shall be no guilt of bloodshed for him.
If the sun has risen on him, he is guilty of bloodshed. He shall make restitution. If he has nothing, then he shall be sold for his theft.
